_about: Mars overlay, deep-merged over data/text.json. Strings marked [placeholder] are stubs: campaign and screens (M4) own the screens text, integration (M6) the night and storm notices, M5 the survey and milestone text.

landing.briefing: [placeholder] The lander has touched down on the floor of Jezero crater. The rover is deploying.

mission.briefing: [placeholder] Ten sols on Mars. The Sun sets every sol: lights on to keep driving, or sleep until dawn.

marsSoon.heading: Titan: coming soon
marsSoon.body: [placeholder] The Mars mission is complete. Research points carry forward to Titan technology.

night.sunset: Sunset. Lights on to keep driving, or sleep until dawn.
night.noLights: [placeholder] No lights: the rover cannot drive at night.

storm.forecast: [placeholder] Orbital weather report: a dust storm reaches the site in about a sol.
storm.started: [placeholder] Dust storm. Solar power is down to about a third.

survey._owner: M5. Lead ids match data/mars/tuning.json survey.leads. Directions and distances are computed, so the text names none.
survey._sources: Delta: Fassett and Head, GRL 32 (2005), doi.org/10.1029/2005GL023456. Seitah: NASA JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Rover Begins Its First Science Campaign on Mars" (jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-perseverance-rover-begins-its-first-science-campaign-on-mars/). HiRISE scale: uahirise.org/TRA_000823_1720; usgs.gov/news/mars-2020-mission-be-guided-usgs-astrogeology-maps.
survey.intro: Orbital data from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter show three areas of interest near the landing site. Directions and distances are measured from the lander and are approximate: orbital maps locate areas, not exact sites. The rover's own survey locates each site; until then, an arrow at the edge of the map points toward each area.

delta.name: Delta front
delta.source: Orbital images show the fan of an ancient river delta, first described as a delta built into a crater lake in 2005. Its front is a cliff where the layers are exposed.

seitah.name: Séítah
seitah.source: HiRISE images show ridged rock with sand ripples between the ridges; the ripples are soft ground. Séítah means "amidst the sand" in the Navajo language.

rocks.name: Boulder field
rocks.source: HiRISE images, at about 25 cm per pixel, show a rough patch of boulders on the crater floor.

instruments._owner: M5: Mars overrides of the shared instrument notices, plus the sunset notices (rules/marsTypes.ts MarsInstrumentText).
instruments.photoNoZone: Photograph added to the album. Milestones count only at viewpoints, or with the setting Sun low in view.
instruments.sunsetHint: The setting Sun is low in view. Press C to take a photograph.
instruments.sunsetTooHigh: The Sun is in view but still high. The sunset photo counts once it is within {max}° of the horizon.
instruments.sunsetTooClose: The setting Sun is in view, but the rover is only {distance} m from the lander. The sunset photo counts at least {min} m away.
